To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the role of scientists is to provide information to policy makers, that the role of science in natural resources policy development is episodic, and that the episodic approach to policy development does not provide the best opportunity for scientists to influence natural resources management policy.
scientific information has a significant influence on policy development and that the episodic model of science in policy development is the best description of the way science is used.
the role of science in resource policy is episodic and that the episodic model of science is less effective than the adaptive model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of science in resource policy development.
the role of science in resource policy and management, the nature of scientific information, and how scientific information is utilized in resource management.
the relationship between science and public policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of scientific information in policy development and implementation is episodic, that the role of the scientific community in this process is limited, and that the scientific information is not used in a systematic or consistent manner.

the use of science in the policy process is not a simple matter and that, in the case of estuarine resource management, the use of science can only be understood in the context of a complex, adaptive, policy-making process.
science has a role in the policy process, but that the role of science is episodic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scientists are important actors in the initiation of policy but their influence declines as policy moves through the development process.
science is important to policy, but it is not the whole story.
the episodic model of scientific information is a useful model of science in natural resource management, but it has limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the episodic model of science in the policy process should be replaced by a model in which science is continuously engaged in the policy process, and in which science and policy are seen as interwoven.
the role of science is to provide a framework for the management of estuaries, not to dictate policy.

the role of science in policy development is more complex than is generally assumed and that the role of scientists is to provide policy makers with a range of options and a range of possible outcomes, rather than a specific solution.
